description: Curated Judicial Evolution notes for Learn (not Bare Act text).

entries.heading: Early interpretation
entries.body: Statutory right only. The Supreme Court historically called the right to vote a "creature of statute" — governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1950, not an absolute fundamental guarantee.

entries.heading: ADR vs Union of India — 2002
entries.body: Voters’ right to information recognised. The Supreme Court held that voters have a constitutional right to know the background of candidates contesting elections.

entries.heading: PUCL vs Union of India — 2003
entries.body: Upgraded to "constitutional right." Justice P.V. Reddy observed that the right to vote, if not a fundamental right, is certainly a constitutional right under Article 326.

entries.heading: PUCL vs Union of India — 2013
entries.body: NOTA introduced. The Supreme Court directed the introduction of the "None of the Above" option to protect voter choice and secrecy — the most recent major judicial expansion of voting rights.
